all_tasks.description:
Bug: has_input_text() in tmux.rs:825 treats Claude Code's placeholder text (e.g. 'How can I help you?') as real user input. This causes wait_for_empty_input() to block for the full 90-second LEAD_INPUT_WAIT_TIMEOUT before delivering every lead nudge.

Root cause: tmux capture-pane renders placeholder text as regular characters — there's no visual distinction from real input in the capture output.

Fix approach: Use tmux cursor position (via 'tmux display-message -p #{cursor_x} #{cursor_y}') as the ground truth for whether the input is empty. If the cursor is at a small cursor_x on the prompt line (right after the prompt symbol), the input is truly empty regardless of any placeholder text being rendered.

Key files:
- src/tmux.rs:825 — has_input_text() needs to be updated
- src/tmux.rs:850 — wait_for_empty_input() uses has_input_text()
- src/coworker.rs:845 — lead_nudge_worker() calls wait_for_empty_input()
- src/coworker.rs:18 — LEAD_INPUT_WAIT_TIMEOUT (90s)

Steps:
1. Write a failing test reproducing the bug — has_input_text returns true when cursor position shows empty input
2. Add a cursor-position-based check to has_input_text (or a new function)
3. Update wait_for_empty_input to use the cursor check
4. Verify the test passes
5. Test that real user input is still correctly detected (don't break the protection against clobbering typed text)
all_tasks.subject: Fix lead nudge delay caused by Claude Code placeholder text

all_tasks.description:
UX improvement: In the chat TUI (src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/mod.rs), typing should always go to the input field, like Slack/Discord.

Current behavior: Character keys only go to the input field when focused_pane == FocusedPane::InputBar. When focus is on Board or Chat, letters like j/k/q/s/g/G act as navigation shortcuts, and other characters are silently dropped.

Desired behavior: When the user starts typing printable characters (that aren't navigation shortcuts), auto-focus the InputBar and route the keystroke there. The 'type anywhere' pattern.

Key file: src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/mod.rs — handle_event() function around line 336.

Design considerations:
- Navigation shortcuts (j/k/q/s/g/G, PageUp/Down, arrows) should still work when NOT in InputBar
- But regular character input (letters, numbers, punctuation) that isn't a bound shortcut should auto-switch focus to InputBar and insert the character
- Backspace/Delete could also auto-focus InputBar if there's text in the input
- Enter should auto-focus InputBar (and submit if there's text)
- This may require rethinking which keys are shortcuts vs. input — e.g., 'j' and 'k' are currently scroll shortcuts, but a user typing 'just a message' would want 'j' to go to the input field
- One approach: only treat single modifier-less letter keys as shortcuts when a modifier like Ctrl is held, or use a vim-like mode (normal/insert). Another: keep current shortcuts but have a short list of 'command' keys and route everything else to input. Look at how similar TUI chat apps handle this.

Write tests for the new key routing behavior.
all_tasks.subject: TUI: Route all typing to input field regardless of focus

all_tasks.description:
Bug: The chat input field in Channel.svelte is not visible when using the web app as a PWA on mobile, but works fine on desktop Chrome.

Layout chain:
- App.svelte: .app has height: 100vh / 100dvh → .channel-main has flex: 1, overflow: hidden
- Channel.svelte: .channel-container has height: 100%, display: flex, flex-direction: column → .messages has flex: 1 → .input-area has flex-shrink: 0

The input-area already has safe-area-inset-bottom padding (line 733). The likely culprit is the mobile-only channel bar at the top (App.svelte line 168) pushing content down without the flex container accounting for it, causing the input to overflow below the visible area.

Possible causes to investigate:
1. Mobile channel bar takes extra height not accounted for in the flex layout
2. iOS standalone PWA viewport calculation differs from Safari — 100dvh may not include the home indicator area correctly
3. field-sizing: content on textarea may not be supported on mobile Safari (check compat)
4. The container may need explicit mobile height calculation: calc(100dvh - mobile-bar-height - env(safe-area-inset-top) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom))

Key files:
- web-app/src/lib/Channel.svelte — .channel-container, .input-area styles
- web-app/src/App.svelte — .channel-main, .mobile-channel-bar, viewport height

IMPORTANT: This project uses viewport-fit=cover and apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes (index.html lines 5-7). Test with Playwright mobile emulation if possible, but the real test is on an actual iOS device in PWA standalone mode.

Include before/after screenshots in the PR (per CLAUDE.md guidelines for visual changes).

Root cause investigation needed:

2. The RPC client times out but the server still processes the request — this is a classic at-most-once vs at-least-once delivery problem.
3. Consider idempotency: task create with the same subject within a short window should deduplicate.

Check daemon logs (RUST_LOG=midtown=debug) for clues about what was happening at the time. The daemon had 5 coworkers in_progress and was handling orphan warnings repeatedly.

all_tasks.description:
The kanban.data RPC handler (src/daemon/rpc.rs:2079 handle_kanban_data) executes a full GraphQL query on every call with no caching. The web UI polls /api/status every 10 seconds, each triggering a fresh GraphQL query. The kanban query is extremely expensive (~200 points per call due to nested first:100 for comments and statusCheckRollup contexts within first:100 for pullRequests). At 360 calls/hour, this alone can consume ~72,000 points against a 5,000-point/hour GraphQL limit.

Fix: Add a TTL cache (30s) inside handle_kanban_data so repeated calls within the TTL return cached results. This matches the web server's CACHE_TTL. The cache should store the serialized response and only re-fetch from GitHub when expired.

Also reduce the nested limits: comments(first: 10) and contexts(first: 20) would cut query cost ~25x while still returning enough data for the kanban board.

Also consider bumping the web UI poll interval from 10s to 30s (web-app/src/lib/api.js:134) to match the cache TTL.
all_tasks.subject: Add daemon-side caching for kanban GraphQL RPC

all_tasks.description: The PR poll (src/daemon/pr.rs:274) fetches comments for ALL open PRs on every 30s poll. This is expensive in GraphQL points due to nested first:100. all_tasks.description:
The daemon becomes unresponsive to RPC calls for 10-30+ seconds during startup when processing pending tasks.

Root cause: execute_effects() runs sequentially in the main event loop, holding persistent_state lock repeatedly across multiple spawn effects.

Three compounding bottlenecks:
1. Sequential spawns in effect loop — each AssignAndSpawn is awaited before the next (100-500ms per spawn + 1-5s per worktree creation)
2. persistent_state.lock() acquired per-effect inside execute_effects(), blocking concurrent RPC handlers that need the same lock
3. Synchronous send_and_broadcast() in main loop uses blocking fs2 file locks (up to 2s), stalling the tokio thread

Fix approach (in priority order):
- Batch persistent_state mutations: collect all state changes from the effect batch, then apply in a single lock acquisition at the end
- Parallelize spawn effects: use tokio::spawn for AssignAndSpawn effects rather than sequential awaiting
- Convert remaining synchronous send_and_broadcast() calls in the main select loop to use send_and_broadcast_async()

Key files: src/daemon/effects.rs (execute_effects loop), src/daemon/mod.rs (main select loop, send_and_broadcast), src/daemon/snapshot.rs (collect_world_snapshot lock pattern)
all_tasks.subject: Fix daemon RPC unresponsiveness during startup

all_tasks.description:
From PR #846 review (vernon), several issues need follow-up:

1. **Overly broad zombie cleanup** — kill_zombie_claude_processes() in startup.rs uses `pgrep -f 'claude.*headless'` which could kill processes from other midtown projects or user sessions. Use a more specific pattern (e.g., match on the project-specific working directory or midtown agent env var).

2. **Shutdown error handling** — persist_sessions_for_restart() uses `?` propagation, so a persistence failure skips detach_all() and sessions are killed instead of surviving. The detach should happen regardless of persistence success.

3. **PID reuse risk** — Recovery kills persisted PIDs without verifying the process is actually a claude process. Add process name/cmdline verification before killing.

4. **Premature state clearing** — headless_sessions is cleared from persistent state before recovery effects execute, creating a crash window where metadata is lost. Clear after effects succeed.

5. **Impure effect generation** — recover_headless_sessions() mixes I/O with Vec<Effect> return. Refactor to follow the pure-decision pattern (collect state into snapshot, return effects without I/O).

Key file: src/daemon/startup.rs
all_tasks.subject: Fix session survival safety issues (from PR #846 review)

to:

all_tasks.description:
midtown channel post and midtown status are hitting 5-second read timeouts when the daemon is busy.

Root causes identified:

1. **handle_status calls gh pr list on every invocation** (src/daemon/rpc.rs:2081) — this is a synchronous GitHub API call via spawn_blocking. Under rate limiting or API slowness, it exceeds the 5s client timeout. The daemon already polls PRs every 30s — serve cached PR data from WorldSnapshot/PersistentState instead of re-fetching.

2. **Client timeout is 5s for everything** (src/bin/midtown/client/mod.rs:116) — hooks need tight timeouts since they block Claude Code, but CLI commands (channel post, status, task create) could use 15-30s. Split the timeout: keep 5s for hook-context calls, use a longer timeout for CLI commands.

3. **spawn_blocking pool contention** — handle_channel_post uses send_and_broadcast_async (spawn_blocking for file I/O). Multiple concurrent gh CLI calls in spawn_blocking can delay file I/O tasks.

Fix approach:
- Replace get_open_prs() in handle_status with cached PR data from the daemon's existing PR polling (WorldSnapshot or PersistentState)
- Same for get_merged_prs() — use cached data
- Add a timeout parameter or context flag to DaemonClient so CLI vs hook callers can specify different timeouts
- Consider whether get_all_tasks() (reads Claude Code task files) should also be cached
all_tasks.subject: Fix RPC read timeouts on midtown CLI commands

all_tasks.description:
When a reviewer coworker is manually broken (midtown coworker break), the daemon doesn't clear the review assignment from GitHubState. It then detects the PR still needs review, sees no active reviewer, and respawns one — creating a loop.

Observed: Broke amsterdam (was reviewing PR #837). Daemon immediately posted 'Restarted stuck reviewer amsterdam for PR #837 (no events for 300s)' and respawned it.

Expected: Breaking a reviewer should clear the review assignment so the daemon doesn't respawn.

Root cause (from madison's review of PR #867): handle_coworker_break in rpc.rs is missing several cleanup steps that exist in shutdown_coworker_impl in effects.rs:
- Cooldown entries
- Pending nudges  
- Task assignments
- Worktree unbind
- Coworker records
- **Reviewer PR assignments** (the specific cause of the respawn loop)

Recent commits 877ff08 and db1c31b added these cleanups to the shutdown path but the break path was not updated. Fix should unify the cleanup logic so both paths share the same cleanup steps.
all_tasks.subject: Fix reviewer respawn after manual break

all_tasks.description:

Simple linear flows, obvious architectures, or diagrams that just restate the text should not be generated. Add guidance to agents/common.md or agents/coworker.md.

2. **Channel-level fix**: Even when diagrams are generated, coworker subagent output (from senders like 'architect') should not land in the main channel. Options:
   a. Filter messages from known subagent senders — route to topic channel only
   b. Don't post subagent output to the channel at all
   c. Only cross-post subagent insights (not diagrams) to the main channel

Observed: Three large mermaid diagrams from 'architect' appeared in the main channel during normal coworker work on tasks !1054 and !1058. These were simple architecture diagrams that restated what was already clear from the task description.

all_tasks.description:
Bug: The daemon repeatedly tries to spawn a coworker for an assigned task every 5 seconds when the coworker is already active on another task. The spawn fails but the daemon doesn't track this and retries indefinitely.

Captured snapshot: snapshot-broadway-spawn-loop-20260210-040327.json

Root cause: The dispatch logic sees a pending task assigned to a coworker and emits a SpawnCoworker effect, but doesn't check if the coworker is already alive/busy. Since the spawn fails (coworker already exists), the task stays pending and the next tick tries again.

Fix approach: Before emitting SpawnCoworker, check if the coworker is already alive in the WorldSnapshot. If so, either nudge them about the new task instead of spawning, or skip and wait for them to become idle.

Write a failing test using the captured snapshot, then fix the bug.
all_tasks.subject: Fix daemon spawn loop when coworker is already active

all_tasks.description:
Bug: When a coworker is spawned to address review feedback on a PR but dies (e.g., from API errors), the daemon never retries. The work is silently dropped.

Root cause (two issues in collect_green_with_feedback_effects in src/daemon/pr.rs):
1. PrIssueTracker cooldown blocks re-nudging after the first spawn attempt. Once the cooldown fires, the PR is skipped on subsequent ticks even if the spawned coworker died.
2. No detection of 'coworker died with unaddressed review feedback' — the daemon doesn't check whether the originally-spawned coworker is still alive and whether the feedback was actually addressed.

Fix approach: After cooldown expires, re-check whether the review feedback was actually addressed (i.e., new commits pushed after the review). If not, and the assigned coworker is dead/idle, reset the tracker and retry. Alternatively, clear the cooldown entry when a coworker dies so the next poll tick re-evaluates.

Related: This is the same family of bugs as !1062 (triple reviewer) and !1066 (spawn loop) — all involve gaps in the daemon's spawning/retry logic.
all_tasks.subject: Fix daemon retry for unaddressed review feedback after coworker death

Wire up the channel clusterer as a resumable headless session in the daemon.

Trigger: When a new task is created (detected via task creation RPC or effect), the daemon invokes the clusterer.

Flow:
1. First task: Daemon spawns a headless session with the clusterer system prompt, sends the task context, gets a JSON diff response, session exits and saves to disk. Store the session ID in DaemonState.
2. Subsequent tasks: Resume the session (claude --resume <session-id> -p ...), send new task + channel state, get diff, session exits.

Message content sent to clusterer:
- New task subject and description
- Current channel list with their active task count and subjects (compact)
- Recently completed tasks (for archive/merge signals)

Use HeadlessSession with haiku model. The session accumulates clustering context across invocations — it remembers previous decisions so it can assign related tasks to existing channels.

Store clusterer_session_id in persistent daemon state so it survives restarts.

4. assign_tasks: Update task_channel mapping in daemon state, call apply_task_channel_mapping() for each assignment

all_tasks.description:
## Problem
Tasks get auto-completed when coworkers report WorkflowPhase::Completed (rpc.rs:1239), which happens after opening a PR but BEFORE review feedback is addressed. This causes:
- Coworker goes idle → gets auto-shutdown → loses session context
- Review feedback has to use HandoffToCoworker (different coworker, no context) or SpawnOwner (session resume, fragile)
- The user explicitly wants: 'address review issues to use the same session as what was used to do the original task'

## Root cause
Three paths complete tasks: (1) WorkflowPhase::Completed via RPC, (2) PR merge detection in dispatch.rs, (3) manual midtown task done. Path 1 fires too early.

## Fix
1. **Store task→PR mapping in persistent state** — Add task_id to PrAuthorSession in github_state.rs (or a parallel HashMap<String, u64> for task_id→pr_number). This must be disk-persisted to survive daemon restarts. When StorePrAuthorSession fires (daemon/mod.rs:1782), also record which task_id the PR is associated with. The PR title already contains [Midtown !XXX] — parse that to get the task_id.

2. **rpc.rs:1239** — Don't auto-complete task on WorkflowPhase::Completed if the task has an associated open PR (check the persisted task→PR mapping). Only auto-complete for PR-less tasks (reviews, investigations). This is the key change.

3. **coworker.md prompt** — After opening PR, coworkers should report pull-request then idle, NOT completed. Stay associated with the task through the review cycle.

4. **Idle shutdown protection** — Ensure coworkers with open PRs are NOT auto-shutdown while waiting for review. (Check if review_feedback_pr_coworkers already handles this.)

5. **effects.rs:204 comment** — Fix stale comment that says 'when its PR is opened'.

6. **dispatch.rs** — PR merge path (lines 830-848) is already correct and stays as the primary completion path for PR-producing tasks.

## Key architecture decision
Tasks that produce PRs complete on MERGE, not on coworker phase transition. Tasks without PRs (review, investigation) complete via midtown task done. The WorkflowPhase::Completed → CompleteTask path in rpc.rs should be conditional, checking the persisted task→PR mapping.
all_tasks.subject: Fix task completion timing: keep coworker sessions alive through PR review cycle

all_tasks.description:
## Root Cause
Headless coworkers load plugins from TWO sources:
1. $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json (auth profile) — 8 plugins
2. --settings coworker-settings.json — 15 plugins (includes the same 8)

The tmux path avoids this with --setting-sources project,local (excludes user-level settings). The headless path (headless.rs) does NOT pass --setting-sources, so plugins are loaded from both sources.

This causes double-initialization of plugins. The session works initially (deduplication handles it), but after idle→resume when the system prompt is re-generated, the tool list breaks and the API returns 400 'tools: Tool names must be unique' (44 tools with duplicates).

## Fix
1. Add a setting_sources field to HeadlessConfig in headless.rs
2. In LaunchConfig::to_headless_config() (launch.rs:186), propagate restrict_setting_sources:
   - When true, set setting_sources to Some('project,local')
3. In HeadlessSession::spawn() (headless.rs), pass --setting-sources when the field is set
4. Write a test that verifies headless coworker config includes --setting-sources

## Evidence
Debug log: ~/.midtown/auth/ben@btucker.net/debug/17d77001-086f-41ca-be7f-667d32acd97f.txt
- Line 354: Plugin pr-review-toolkit loaded TWICE (13:26:05 and 13:26:06)
- Line 5404: Stop/TeammateIdle at 13:40:03
- Line 5414: [SystemPrompt] path=simple at 13:40:35 (resume after nudge)
- Line 5418: ERROR 'Tool names must be unique' at 13:40:36 (44 tools)
all_tasks.subject: Fix 'Tool names must be unique' API error in headless coworkers

all_tasks.description:
Captured snapshot: snapshot-reviewer-not-spawning-20260210-182655.json

After a daemon crash and restart, idle coworkers were not being assigned to review open PRs. The daemon kept warning 'PR #X has been open for N minutes with no review — I assigned a reviewer but no review has been posted yet' but wasn't spawning new reviewers.

Root cause investigation found: Reviewer coworkers are spawned with session_id: null. This causes:
1. backfill_reviewer_session_ids() in github_state.rs (line 364-368) filters out coworkers without session_id, so backfill fails
2. Assignments eventually expire after 600 seconds via cleanup_expired_preserving()
3. After cleanup, PRs show as needing review but the daemon may not re-spawn reviewers if the stale state (from the pre-cleanup snapshot) still shows them as assigned
4. The WorldSnapshot is collected ONCE at tick start (snapshot.rs), so cleanup during the tick and spawning decisions may see different states

Key files:
- src/daemon/pr.rs lines 231-404 (cleanup), 1630-1880 (spawning)
- src/github_state.rs lines 265-385 (assignment tracking), 395-410 (is_assigned), 501-509 (cleanup_expired_preserving)  
- src/daemon/snapshot.rs lines 387-409 (active_reviewers, reviewer_pr_assignments)
- src/session_manager.rs (session_id reporting)

Expected: After restart, daemon should detect that reviewer sessions are dead and re-assign reviewers
Actual: Daemon warns about missing reviews but doesn't spawn new reviewers for several minutes

Write a failing E2E test using the captured snapshot, then fix the bug.

York's review of PR #908 found the fix doesn't actually work:

**Problem**: persistent_state.headless_sessions is drained by recover_headless_sessions() during startup and only repopulated at shutdown. The new sync_with_tmux() logic in the fix iterates an always-empty map during normal operation, so session_id restoration never executes. **Root cause**: The fix assumed headless_sessions would be populated during normal operation, but it's only a persistence mechanism (populated at shutdown, consumed at startup).

**Needed**: A different approach to restore session_ids for recovered coworkers. Options:
1. Don't drain headless_sessions during recovery — keep a copy available for sync_with_tmux
2. Store session_id mapping in a separate field that persists past startup
3. Have recovered sessions re-register their session_id via RPC after recovery

Review comment: https://github.com/btucker/midtown/pull/908#issuecomment-3880075329

Fix this on the existing PR #908 branch, ensure the test actually exercises the real startup path, push, and go idle.

Lead committed changes on branch lead/task-lifecycle-complete-on-merge. Open a PR, get it reviewed, and merge.

## Changes
The branch implements the 'Task Lifecycle: Complete on Merge' plan:

1. **Prevent premature completion** (rpc.rs): When a coworker reports Completed without an open PR, nudge them to open a PR instead of auto-completing the task
2. **Unassign tasks in review** (tasks.rs, effects.rs, dispatch.rs, snapshot.rs): New reconcile_tasks_in_review() runs each tick — clears task owner on disk when PR is open and coworker is inactive, freeing the name for new work
3. **Handle abandoned PRs** (pr.rs, effects.rs): During PR polling, detect closed-without-merge PRs and reset associated tasks to pending
4. **Fix stale comment** (tasks.rs): Updated misleading doc comment
5. **Update coworker.md**: Instruct go-idle after PR instead of reporting completed

New Effect variants: UnassignTask, ResetAbandonedTask
New WorldSnapshot field: tasks_with_open_prs (task_id → pr_number from PrAuthorSession)
New function: tasks::unassign_task_for_repo()

## Tests
- 4 unit tests for reconcile_tasks_in_review (inactive owner, active owner, no PR, empty owner)
- 2 unit tests in tasks.rs (unassign preserves status, busy_coworkers excludes unowned)
- All existing tests pass, clippy clean

The test `test_unread_count_calculation` in `src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/app.rs:2560` is flaky on CI. It panics with:

```
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Io(Custom { kind: WouldBlock, error: "lock acquisition failed because the operation would block" })
```

**Root cause**: `Channel::read_all()` uses non-blocking `try_lock_shared()` (to avoid TUI freezes). On CI, brief lock contention between sequential `send()` and `read_all()` calls causes `WouldBlock` errors.

**Fix**: The test calls `channel.read_all().unwrap()` directly (line 2622). The channel.rs test helpers already have `read_all_with_retry()` for exactly this. Either:
1. Import/replicate the retry helper in app.rs tests and use it here, OR
2. Add a small retry loop around the `read_all()` call in the test

Also check that `refresh_unread_counts()` (called at lines 2585, 2609, 2634) handles `WouldBlock` gracefully since it calls `message_count()` -> `read_all()` internally (it currently silently swallows errors via `Err(_) => continue`, which is fine).

**Failing CI runs**: 21887230903 and 21888646333 (both on main).

This is blocking main CI — fix ASAP.

all_tasks.description:
The complete-on-merge feature only closes tasks when a merged PR title contains [Midtown !XXXX] matching the task ID. This misses several common patterns:

1. **Meta-tasks** — e.g. 'Merge reviewed PRs: #901-#910' with no single PR tagged to it
2. **Sub-tasks** — e.g. 'Address PR #904 review feedback' where PR #904 is tagged with a different task
3. **Fix-PR tasks** — e.g. 'Fix PR #908' where PR #908 is tagged [Midtown !1099], not the fix task ID

These stale tasks accumulate and confuse the daemon's assignment logic.

**Possible approaches (pick one or combine):**
- Close tasks when their owning coworker goes idle/on-break with no open PR and the task has been in_progress for a while
- Parse task descriptions for PR references (#NNN) and close the task when all referenced PRs are merged
- When a coworker reports idle, check if their in_progress tasks have any remaining work (open PRs, uncommitted changes) — if not, auto-complete
- Add a staleness heuristic: if a task has been in_progress with no channel activity from the owner for N minutes, mark it for review

The fix should happen in rules.rs (pure decision logic) returning Effect variants, consistent with the architecture.
all_tasks.subject: Improve task auto-completion for indirect task-PR relationships

all_tasks.description:
The orphan worktree detector repeatedly warns about worktrees (amsterdam, park, columbus, madison) whose commits are already merged to main via squash merge. This happens because the detector compares commit SHAs, but squash merges produce different SHAs on main.

**Symptoms:** Repeated warnings like 'Orphaned worktrees with unmerged commits (not on any PR): amsterdam, park' even though all their work has landed.

**Root cause:** The detector checks if worktree commits exist on main by SHA, but squash-merged commits have different SHAs.

**Possible fixes:**
1. Use `git cherry` or `git log --cherry-pick` to detect equivalent commits regardless of SHA
2. Check if the worktree's branch has an associated merged PR (via GitHub API or local tracking)
3. Compare commit messages / patch IDs instead of SHAs
4. When a coworker goes on break with no open PR and no pending task, consider the worktree clean

This is high-frequency noise that drowns out real issues in the channel. The detection logic is likely in rules.rs or a related module.
all_tasks.subject: Fix orphan worktree detector false positives for squash-merged commits

**Symptoms:** Every API request returns 400 with 'tools: Tool names must be unique'. Coworkers spin forever retrying. The daemon detects API errors but can't recover because the sessions themselves are corrupted (duplicate tool registrations).

**Expected behavior:** The daemon should detect this unrecoverable error pattern (400 with duplicate tools) and shut down + respawn the affected coworkers rather than letting them spin.

**Two fixes needed:**
1. **Root cause**: Prevent duplicate tool registration in session resume (what PR #930 attempted)
2. **Safety net**: Daemon should detect coworkers stuck in API error retry loops and force-restart them

Write a failing E2E test using the captured snapshot, then fix both issues.
all_tasks.subject: Fix 'Tool names must be unique' error causing all coworkers to brick

**Fix:** In the orphan recovery logic, before re-assigning a coworker to an orphaned task, check if any PR tagged with [Midtown !<task_id>] has already been merged. If so, complete the task instead of recovering a coworker for it.

This is a safety net complementing task !1127 (auto-completion). Even if auto-completion works perfectly, recovery should still verify.

When a field is set to None in the struct, merge_tables() leaves the old value in the TOML because it only overlays present keys.

Add a generic removal pass that removes keys from the target table that are not present in the new serialized table, with care for comment-only sections that should be preserved.

Applies to both GlobalConfig::save() and FullProjectConfig::save_to().

See PR #937 review comment: https://github.com/btucker/midtown/pull/937#issuecomment-3881867065
all_tasks.subject: Generic None-removal for merge_tables() across all Option<T> fields

Do a thorough sweep of the entire src/ directory and identify code simplification opportunities. Focus on:

1. **Overly complex functions** — functions that are too long, have too many branches, or do too many things

3. **Dead code** — unused functions, structs, enum variants, imports
4. **Over-abstraction** — abstractions that aren't earning their complexity (e.g., traits with one impl, generic wrappers around single types)
5. **Tangled responsibilities** — modules or functions that mix concerns and could be split or reorganized
6. **Unnecessary indirection** — layers that just forward calls without adding value

For each opportunity found, report:
- File and function/struct name
- What the issue is
- Rough complexity reduction (high/medium/low impact)
- Any risks or dependencies to watch out for

all_tasks.description:
Add a --model <provider/model> flag to `midtown task create` and `midtown task update` commands. Format: `<provider>/<model>` (e.g., `claude/opus`, `claude/sonnet`).

**Storage**: Add `task_model: HashMap<String, String>` to `DaemonPersistentState` in `src/daemon/state.rs`. This keeps model preferences separate from Claude Code's native task storage in `~/.claude/tasks/` for compatibility. Follow the same pattern as `task_channel: HashMap<String, String>` which already maps task ID → channel name.

**Spawn behavior**: When the daemon builds a `LaunchConfig` for a coworker assigned to a task, check `task_model` for that task ID. If set, split on `/` — the provider part (e.g., `claude`) determines which CLI to invoke, the model part (e.g., `opus`) gets passed as `--model` to the worker. Only the model part goes to `--model`, NOT the full `provider/model` string. The `LaunchConfig.model` field already accepts values like `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku` — just override it with the model portion.

**Implementation**:
1. Add `task_model: HashMap<String, String>` field to `DaemonPersistentState` (with `#[serde(default)]`)
2. Add `--model <PROVIDER/MODEL>` flag to `task create` and `task update` CLI commands
3. Add RPC endpoint(s) so the CLI can store/update the model preference in daemon state
4. In dispatch.rs where `LaunchConfig` is built for task spawning, look up `task_model` and override `LaunchConfig.model` with the model portion
5. Surface the model in `midtown task view` output
6. Add the model info to the WorldSnapshot so decision functions can see it

**Validation**: provider/model format should be enforced (must contain exactly one `/`). Known providers for now: `claude`, `codex`. Known models: `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `o3`, `o4-mini`.

Write tests first.
all_tasks.subject: Add --model flag to task create/update CLI with separate storage

all_tasks.description:
midtown restart should by default wait for all coworkers to reach a clean stopping point before shutting down the daemon. Current behavior kills everything immediately.

Proposed flow:
1. Stop assigning new tasks
2. Signal all coworkers to finish current work
3. Print real-time drain status to the terminal:
   ```
   Waiting for coworkers to finish...
     amsterdam: working on !1158 (Auto-clean worktrees...)
     broadway: idle ✓
     york: working on !1156 (Add --model flag...)
     broadway stopped.
     amsterdam: idle ✓
     amsterdam stopped.
     york: idle ✓
     york stopped.
   All coworkers stopped. Restarting daemon...
   Daemon started.
   ```
4. Once all coworkers are idle/stopped, shut down daemon
5. Restart daemon (coworkers get resumed via --resume as needed)

The user should always know what's happening — who's still draining, who's done.

Consider: timeout for coworkers that don't stop within a reasonable window (force-kill as fallback). And a --force flag to skip the wait for urgent restarts.

all_tasks.description:
The clusterer infrastructure exists but is not wired to the daemon event loop. Two things need to happen:

## 1. Wire up the existing clusterer

Connect `src/daemon/clusterer.rs` and `src/daemon/clustering.rs` to the daemon event loop. The code exists, the system prompt is at `agents/clusterer.md`, and the effect pipeline (`apply_clustering_diff() -> Vec<Effect>`) follows the pure-function pattern. Just needs to be called when new tasks are created.

## 2. Implement dual-channel model

Two types of channels, inspired by Slack conventions:

### Durable channels (no prefix)
- Map to architectural domains of the project: `github-integration`, `tui`, `web-interface`, `daemon-core`, `sandbox`, etc.
- Persist for the lifetime of the project (or until architecture changes)
- Created by the clusterer on first analysis of the codebase, re-evaluated periodically
- Never archived just because tasks complete — only archived if that architectural area no longer exists
- Tasks get assigned to these based on which part of the architecture they touch

### Project channels (`#proj-` prefix)  
- Ephemeral, tied to a specific initiative or body of work in flight
- Examples: `#proj-sandbox-fix`, `#proj-graceful-restart`
- Archived when all tasks complete and related PRs merge
- This is roughly what the current clusterer agent prompt already describes

### Clusterer changes needed
- Update `agents/clusterer.md` to understand both channel types
- Add periodic re-evaluation of durable channels (e.g., on a timer tick, not just on new task creation)
- Initial durable channel creation should analyze the codebase structure (file tree, module boundaries) to propose architectural channels
- The ClusteringDiff format may need a new field to distinguish channel types, or channel names could encode it via the prefix convention

### Key files
- `src/daemon/clusterer.rs` — session management (exists, not wired)
- `src/daemon/clustering.rs` — pure decision logic (exists, dead code)
- `src/clustering.rs` — data structures
- `agents/clusterer.md` — system prompt
- `src/daemon/mod.rs` / `src/daemon/events.rs` — wiring point
all_tasks.subject: Wire up clusterer and implement dual-channel model (durable + #proj-)
Handle relative gitdir paths in sandbox worktree detection

Root cause: confusion between CoworkerStatus (lifecycle: Starting/Running/Stopping/Stopped) and WorkflowPhase (activity: Idle/Developing/Testing/etc.). When a coworker reports WorkflowPhase::Idle, the daemon shuts it down immediately (Stopping → Stopped), so CoworkerStatus is never "idle".

The drain loop should check CoworkerStatus for Stopped (or not Running), not for "idle". Fix the condition and remove the misleading comment.

all_tasks.description:
Phase 4 core: Wire up daemon message routing to topic channels.

Currently send_and_broadcast() writes all messages to self.channel (the main channel). The clusterer assigns tasks to channels but messages don't actually route there.

Three tightly coupled pieces:

1. **Task-to-channel mapping in daemon state** — Store the clusterer's task-channel assignments in DaemonPersistentState so the daemon knows which channel a task belongs to.

2. **Daemon message routing** — When a coworker posts a message, look up their current task's channel assignment and write to that channel file (channels/<name>.jsonl) instead of the main channel. send_and_broadcast() needs a channel parameter or should resolve it from context.

3. **Coworker messages routed to topic channels** — Status updates, PR lifecycle, @coworker coordination chatter goes to the topic channel. Only @user mentions, insights (cross-posted), task creation/completion one-liners, errors, and escalations go to the main channel.

Key files: src/channel.rs, src/daemon/effects.rs (send_and_broadcast), src/daemon/state.rs, src/clustering.rs

This is the critical missing piece — once routing works, the rest of Phase 4 falls into place.
all_tasks.subject: Route daemon messages to topic channels based on task-channel assignments

- source_channel set to the topic channel name
- Display format in TUI/web: "#channel-name | author\n  insight content"

This ensures the main channel stays useful as an executive summary — you see all insights without subscribing to every topic channel.

Depends on daemon message routing being functional (task for routing topic channels).

4. **Unread indicators** — track which channels have new messages since last viewed

all_tasks.description:
HIGH PRIORITY — Root cause of duplicate PR creation.

When Effect::CompleteTask executes (PR merged), it marks the task completed and clears the task assignment, but does NOT remove the pr_author_sessions entry for the merged PR. This leaves stale state that causes the daemon to think the task still needs work.

Fix: In effects.rs lines 920-939, when CompleteTask runs, also remove the pr_author_sessions entry for the completed task's PR:
  ps.github.pr_author_sessions.retain(|_, session| session.task_id.as_deref() != Some(&task_id));

This is the single biggest fix — it prevents stale pr_author_sessions from persisting after merges.

Key files: src/daemon/effects.rs (CompleteTask handler), src/github_state.rs (pr_author_sessions)
all_tasks.subject: Fix duplicate PRs: clean up pr_author_sessions on task completion

all_tasks.description:
HIGH PRIORITY — Prevents coworkers from being assigned to tasks that already have open PRs.

should_recover_task() in dispatch.rs:79-143 checks if task.pr is merged but does NOT check pr_task_associations (the task-to-PR mapping from pr_author_sessions). So if a task has an open PR tracked via pr_author_sessions but no explicit task.pr field, orphan recovery will spawn a new coworker.

Fix: In should_recover_task(), also check snap.tasks_with_open_prs. If the task has an open PR via either task.pr OR tasks_with_open_prs, skip orphan recovery.

Key files: src/daemon/dispatch.rs (should_recover_task, check_and_recover_orphans)
all_tasks.subject: Fix duplicate PRs: orphan recovery should check pr_task_associations

all_tasks.description:
MEDIUM PRIORITY — Prevents task reset when a duplicate PR is closed.

detect_abandoned_pr_tasks() in pr.rs:229-261 resets tasks to pending when a PR is closed without merge, but doesn't check if the work was already completed by a DIFFERENT PR. This caused task !1158 to be reset to pending when duplicate PR #999 was closed, even though PR #968 had already merged the work.

Fix: Before resetting a task for an abandoned PR, check:
1. If the task status is already completed
2. If merged_pr_numbers contains any PR associated with this task
3. If the task has an explicit pr field pointing to a merged PR

If any are true, don't reset — the work was already landed.

Key files: src/daemon/pr.rs (detect_abandoned_pr_tasks)
all_tasks.subject: Fix duplicate PRs: abandoned PR detection should check for merged siblings

Implement z.ai as a third auth provider in Midtown (Phases 1-3 of the multi-provider plan).

- Credential detection: check for `api_key.txt` in profile dir
- Add `AuthProviderArg::Zai` variant in main.rs (line 42)

Profile dir structure:
```
~/.midtown/auth/providers/zai/profiles/<email>/
├── api_key.txt      # API key (chmod 600)
└── base_url.txt     # Optional override (default: https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic)
```

## Phase 2: CLI Login + Key Management (src/bin/midtown/cli/auth.rs)

- Extend `handle_login()` with provider-specific branch for `AuthProvider::Zai`:
  - Interactive: prompt for API key via stdin, optional base URL prompt
  - `--key` flag on login subcommand for non-interactive use
  - Write `api_key.txt` with chmod 600, optionally `base_url.txt`
- Add `--key` optional arg to `AuthCommand::Login`

## Phase 3: Launch Configuration (src/launch.rs)

- In `to_headless_config()` (line 213) and `to_shell_command()` (line 277):
  - For `AuthProvider::Zai`: read `api_key.txt` from profile dir → set `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`
  - Read `base_url.txt` or default to `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic` → set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`
  - Don't set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for z.ai
- Helper function: `fn zai_env_vars(profile_dir: &Path) -> HashMap<String, String>`

## Tests

- `src/auth.rs`: provider paths, credential detection, `FromStr` for "zai"
- `src/launch.rs`: headless config sets correct env vars for z.ai, default base URL

## Verification

2. `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` — clean
3. `midtown auth --provider zai login test@z.ai --key sk-xxx` stores key non-interactively
4. `midtown auth list --all-providers` shows z.ai profiles

all_tasks.description:
Implement multi-account usage tracking and display for TUI and web UI (Phases 4-6 of the multi-provider plan). Depends on Task !1202 for z.ai provider but can start with multi-account Claude support.

## Phase 4: Multi-Account Usage Tracking (src/usage.rs, src/daemon/mod.rs, src/daemon/rpc.rs, src/web.rs)

Currently usage is fetched for a single profile. Change to track all active provider/profiles:

- **New struct** `MultiUsageData`: `Vec<UsageData>` where each entry includes `provider` + `profile_name` fields
- **Daemon**: Track which provider/profile combos are active (have running coworkers). Derive from `LaunchConfig.auth_provider` + `auth_profile_dir` of running coworkers.
- **Usage fetching**: Fetch usage for each unique active provider/profile combo. z.ai profiles return `None` initially (no usage API).
- **RPC endpoint** `kanban.data` (already returns coworker info): Include `provider` field per coworker
- **Web endpoint** `/api/usage`: Return array of usage entries instead of single object. Backwards-compat: also keep flat fields for the primary account.

## Phase 5: TUI Multi-Account Usage Display (src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/ui/usage.rs, src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/ui/mod.rs, src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/app.rs)

- `draw_usage_bars()` → `draw_multi_usage_bars()`: iterate over `Vec<UsageData>`, draw stacked pairs
  - Each account: label line (`Claude (user@example.com)` or `z.ai (user@z.ai)`), session bar, weekly bar
  - Accounts with no usage data (z.ai): show label + "No usage data available"
- Layout: dynamically calculate height based on number of active accounts (4 lines per account with data, 2 lines per account without)
- `app.rs`: change `usage_data: Option<UsageData>` → `usage_data: Vec<UsageData>`, update refresh logic to fetch for all active profiles

## Phase 6: Web Multi-Account Usage Display (web-app/src/lib/UsageBars.svelte, web-app/src/lib/store.js, web-app/src/lib/api.js)

- `usageData` store: change from single object to array of `{ provider, profile, session_util, session_resets, week_util, week_resets, account_email }`
- `UsageBars.svelte`: iterate over array, render stacked bar pairs per account
- `api.js:fetchUsage()`: handle array response from `/api/usage`

## Tests

- `src/usage.rs`: multi-usage fetching with mixed providers
- `src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/ui/usage.rs`: rendering with 0, 1, 2+ accounts
- Web: update `usage.test.js` for array format

## Verification

1. `cargo test` — all unit tests pass
2. `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` — clean
3. Verify TUI shows stacked usage bars for active accounts
4. Verify web UI shows stacked usage bars
all_tasks.subject: Multi-provider concurrent usage tracking and display

PR #1070 changed bare `midtown auth` to call `handle_list_all_providers()` which renders a static text table. This lost the interactive TUI selector that `handle_list()` provides (profile switching, add account, remove via keyboard).

**Current behavior:** `midtown auth` shows a flat text table of all providers with no interactivity.

**Expected behavior:** `midtown auth` should show an interactive TUI that lets you:
1. See profiles across all providers (grouped by provider)
2. Select a profile to switch to (with provider context)  
3. Add a new account (prompting for provider)

all_tasks.description:
When coworkers hit HTTP 401 'OAuth token has expired' errors, the daemon currently misdetects this as a usage limit. This causes rapid flapping (nudge → detect limit → wait → nudge → detect limit) because the token won't self-heal like a usage limit reset does.

**What happened:**
- ben@quotably.com OAuth token expired
- Multiple coworkers (park, madison, broadway) entered 401 error loops
- Daemon detected these as 'usage limit' and entered nudge-when-reset cycle
- The cycle flapped every 30-60 seconds because the 401 kept recurring
- Lead had to manually identify the root cause, break coworkers, and ask user to re-auth

**Required behavior:**
1. **Detect auth errors distinctly from usage limits** — when a coworker's pane shows 'OAuth token has expired' or 'authentication_error' (HTTP 401), recognize this as an auth failure, not a usage limit
2. **Notify the lead/user** — post a clear message to the channel: '@user OAuth token expired for <profile>. Run: midtown auth --provider <provider> login <profile>' (or trigger `/login` in the lead session)
3. **Stop retrying** — don't keep nudging coworkers that are stuck on auth errors. Send them on break or pause them until the token is refreshed
4. **After re-auth, relaunch affected coworkers** — once the user re-authenticates, automatically restart coworkers that were paused due to the auth failure

**Key files:**
- src/daemon/health.rs or src/rules.rs — pane scraping / stuck detection logic
- src/daemon/effects.rs — where coworker break/shutdown effects execute
- src/daemon/snapshot.rs — may need a new field to capture auth error state
- src/session_manager.rs — headless session event stream may surface auth errors directly

**Design considerations:**
- Auth errors come through the Claude CLI's stderr/pane output, not through an RPC response
- The daemon already scrapes pane content for stuck detection — extend this to detect auth error patterns
- Consider adding an AuthError variant to the coworker health enum alongside Stuck/Zombie/etc.
- The 'stop retrying' behavior is critical — without it, the flapping loop wastes API calls and generates noise
all_tasks.subject: Detect expired OAuth tokens and prompt user to re-authenticate

After daemon restarts, multiple coworkers get assigned to the same task or to tasks that are already completed. This session saw 5 separate incidents of duplicate work, all restart-related.

Captured snapshot: snapshot-duplicate-work-after-restart-20260212-231938.json

**Three distinct failure modes:**

1. **Tasks with open PRs get reassigned** — When a coworker opens a PR but the task isn't marked 'completed' (waiting for merge), the daemon sees it as an unowned in_progress task after restart and reassigns it. Fix: Before assigning a task, check if there's already an open PR linked to it (via task-PR association or PR title pattern [Midtown !XXX]). If so, mark it as 'has PR' and don't reassign.

2. **Completed tasks revert to pending** — Task completion status may not survive restarts if the completing coworker's session dies before the status is persisted. Fix: Verify task status is written to disk before acknowledging completion.

3. **Multiple reviewers spawned for same PR** — After restart + usage limit recovery, multiple idle coworkers all see 'needs review' and get assigned. Fix: Track reviewer assignment per PR and deduplicate during the assignment phase in rules.rs (check if a reviewer is already assigned/active for that PR before spawning another).

**Key files:**
- src/rules.rs — task assignment and reviewer spawning decisions
- src/daemon/dispatch.rs — task dispatch logic
- src/tasks.rs — task status persistence
- src/daemon/pr.rs — PR review assignment

This is a high-impact issue — duplicate work wastes coworker capacity and creates confusion. Write failing tests using the captured snapshot, then fix.

Bug: The PR polling loop in pr.rs (line 664-669) skips any PR whose branch cannot be mapped to a known coworker via coworker_from_branch_with_map(). all_tasks.description:
## Goal

Change how midtown sets up CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Claude auth profiles so that tasks, history, and other Claude Code state is shared across all auth profiles, while keeping auth credentials (.claude.json) per-profile.

## Current State

- Claude auth profiles live at ~/.midtown/auth/<profile>/ (flat directory)
- CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR points directly to this directory
- Each profile gets its own tasks, history, settings, etc. — they're isolated

## Desired State

### Directory Structure

```
~/.midtown/auth/<profile>/claude/      # CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for this profile
├── .claude.json                        # Real file — per-profile auth credentials
├── tasks -> ~/.midtown/providers/claude/tasks
├── projects -> ~/.midtown/providers/claude/projects  
├── settings.json -> ~/.midtown/providers/claude/settings.json
└── <everything else> -> ~/.midtown/providers/claude/<name>

~/.midtown/providers/claude/            # Shared state across all profiles
├── tasks/
├── projects/
├── settings.json
└── ...
```

### Rules

1. `~/.midtown/auth/<profile>/claude/` is what gets set as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
2. `.claude.json` in that dir is a real file (per-profile auth credentials) — never symlinked
3. Everything else in that dir is a symlink to `~/.midtown/providers/claude/<name>`
4. The shared dir `~/.midtown/providers/claude/` is created on first use if it doesn't exist

### Key Code Changes

1. **src/auth.rs** — `profile_dir_for(AuthProvider::Claude, name)` should return `~/.midtown/auth/<name>/claude/` instead of `~/.midtown/auth/<name>/`
2. **src/auth.rs** — Add a function to ensure the profile dir is set up with proper symlinks (called during profile creation and on launch)
3. **src/auth.rs** or new module — Symlink setup logic: scan the shared dir, create symlinks in the profile dir for everything that isn't .claude.json. Also handle the reverse: if something new appears in the shared dir later, add the symlink.
4. **src/bin/midtown/cli/auth.rs** — `ensure_profile_dir_for()` should call the new setup function
5. **Migration** — When a profile dir exists at the old path (~/.midtown/auth/<profile>/) without the claude/ subdirectory, migrate it:
   - Move .claude.json to ~/.midtown/auth/<profile>/claude/.claude.json
   - Move everything else to ~/.midtown/providers/claude/ (if not already there)
   - Create symlinks from the new profile dir to the shared dir
6. **scripts/e2e-container.sh** — Update the auth dir path if needed

### Important Details

- The existing providers layout (`~/.midtown/auth/providers/codex/`, `~/.midtown/auth/providers/zai/`) stays unchanged — this only affects the Claude provider
- The env var name stays CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (the auth_provider.env_var() mapping doesn't change)
- active_profile_dir_for_project() and related functions should return the new path automatically since they call profile_dir_for()
- Run symlink setup both at profile creation AND at launch time (to pick up new shared files)
- Be careful with the e2e test setup in scripts/e2e-container.sh — it mounts auth dirs into containers
all_tasks.subject: Restructure CLAUDE_CODE_CONFIG_DIR for shared state across auth profiles

all_tasks.description:
## Context

PR #1104 landed a directory layout of ~/.midtown/auth/{profile}/claude/ for Claude auth profiles. The broader auth redesign (see plan at ~/.midtown/projects/midtown/plans/2026-02-13-auth-platform-acp-redesign.md) calls for a provider-first layout to support multiple platforms and providers.

## Change

Update the directory layout from:
```
~/.midtown/auth/{profile}/claude/
~/.midtown/providers/claude/
```

To:
```
~/.midtown/auth/{provider}/{profile}/{platform}/
~/.midtown/providers/{platform}/
```

For now, the only provider is 'anthropic' and the only platform is 'claude', but the structure must support the general case.

### Examples:
- `~/.midtown/auth/anthropic/work@example.com/claude/` — Claude Code config dir for work@example.com via Anthropic
- `~/.midtown/auth/zai/ben@zai/claude/` — Claude Code config dir for ben@zai via z.ai
- `~/.midtown/auth/openai/team-key/codex/` — Codex config dir for team-key via OpenAI
- `~/.midtown/providers/claude/` — Shared state for Claude platform (tasks, history, settings)

### Code changes needed:
1. **src/auth.rs** — Update `profile_dir_for()` to return `~/.midtown/auth/{provider}/{profile}/{platform}/`. The function signature will need both platform and provider params (or a combined type).
2. **src/auth.rs** — Update `provider_profiles_dir()` and related path functions.
3. **src/auth.rs** — Update migration logic to handle both the legacy layout (`~/.midtown/auth/{profile}/`) AND the intermediate layout (`~/.midtown/auth/{profile}/claude/`) from PR #1104. Both should migrate to the new provider-first layout.
4. **src/auth.rs** — Update `ensure_profile_dir_for()` and symlink setup to use new paths.
5. **src/auth.rs** — `shared_provider_dir()` should use `~/.midtown/providers/{platform}/` (may already be correct).
6. **src/bin/midtown/cli/auth.rs** — Update CLI commands (login, switch, remove, list) to work with provider-first paths.
7. **Tests** — Update all auth-related tests for new directory structure.
8. **scripts/e2e-container.sh** — Update auth dir paths if needed.

### Important:
- For now, the current AuthProvider enum can stay (this is just a directory layout change). The full Platform/Provider type split comes in a later phase.
- Map current AuthProvider variants to provider+platform: Claude→(anthropic,claude), Zai→(zai,claude), Codex→(openai,codex)
- Migration must be seamless — existing profiles should just work after the update.
all_tasks.subject: Update auth profile directory layout to provider-first nesting

PR #1088 removed task rows from the TUI Board sidebar, showing only channel names. The user wants them back, with improved status indicators.

## What to restore

The fix is in `src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/ui/board.rs`. The `render_task_item` function and `compute_task_indentation` still exist but are marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` and not called.

What was removed (see git show e5ea30f):
1. The `wrap_width` computation: `let wrap_width = area.width.saturating_sub(2).max(20) as usize;`
2. The loop calling `render_task_item` for each task under each channel header
3. Blank line separator between channels
4. Blank line after each channel header

Restore the task rendering loop. Remove the `#[allow(dead_code)]` annotations from `render_task_item`, `compute_task_indentation`, and `compute_indentation_recursive`. Keep the focus indicator improvements (yellow border) from that same PR — only restore the task rows.

## New: Status indicator changes

1. **Remove** the stoplight emoji (🔴🟡🟢) from the channel header lines entirely.
2. **Change the task bullet** (currently `● ` for in-progress and `○ ` for pending) to use unicode circles with colors based on task+PR state:
   - **Gray circle** — task not started yet (pending, no owner or no work happening)
   - **Brown/yellow circle** — work is in progress (task has an owner working on it)
   - **Green circle** — PR is open and CI checks passed
   - **Red circle** — CI build failure or merge conflict on the PR

Use the same unicode circle character (`●`) for all states, just change the color. Look at how the coworker status table already uses health dots for reference on the color approach.

The task's PR status can be determined by cross-referencing `app.prs` with the task ID (PRs have `[Midtown !XXX]` in the title). Check `pr.ci_status` for CI state and `pr.has_conflicts` (or equivalent) for merge conflicts.

all_tasks.description:
Root cause of 2026-02-13 coworker sandbox nesting failure:

The lead ran `midtown start --daemon-only` from within the lead's tmux session, which runs inside sandbox-exec. This created a new daemon process inheriting the sandbox. All subsequent coworker spawns failed with 'Already inside a sandbox — cannot nest sandbox-exec'.

The exec-restart path (daemon.exec-restart RPC → exec syscall) correctly preserves the original unsandboxed context. But a FRESH start from a sandboxed context has no protection.

Fix options:
1. In the daemon startup path, check `can_sandbox()` — if false, warn loudly that the daemon is running inside a sandbox and coworker sandboxing will be disabled
2. Or: have `midtown start` detect the sandbox and exec itself from a clean context (harder)
3. At minimum: add a prominent warning in the daemon log when sandbox is unavailable

The check should go in `src/daemon/mod.rs` at daemon startup, using `crate::sandbox::can_sandbox()`.
all_tasks.subject: Prevent daemon start inside sandbox

Note: In many terminals, Shift+Enter sends a specific escape sequence (often \x1b[13;2u in kitty protocol, or \x1bOM / \x1b\r in others). The implementation should handle the common terminal encodings for this key combination.
all_tasks.subject: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for multiline message input

!1289 fixes the assignment race, but this task adds a lower-level safety net so that even if future dispatch bugs cause duplicate assignments, the spawn itself is blocked.

- worktree_registry.rs: bind_coworker() (lines ~97-116)
- coworker.rs: prepare_spawn() (lines ~1050-1164)  
- daemon/effects.rs: Effect::BindCoworkerToWorktree handler (lines ~1231-1247)

## Bug
The daemon's `text_contains_review_signature()` in `src/daemon/helpers.rs:372` matches `<!-- midtown:` frontmatter, which ALL coworker GitHub comments include. This means ANY coworker comment on a PR (CI fix explanations, status updates, etc.) is falsely detected as a code review. The PR gets cached as 'reviewed' in `daemon-state.json` and no reviewer is ever assigned.

## Root Cause
Line 372: `text.contains("<!-- midtown:")` - this was intended to detect comment-based reviews (which use midtown frontmatter), but it matches ALL coworker comments.

## Evidence
- PR #1139 has `reviewed_prs: [1139]` in daemon-state.json despite having zero code reviews (cache already cleared manually)
- Columbus posted a CI fix explanation comment with `<!-- midtown: columbus -->` which triggered the false positive
- 5 of the last 10 merged PRs had zero reviews, likely from this same bug

## Approach: Add comment_type to frontmatter
Instead of heuristic text matching, make the comment type explicit in the frontmatter:

- Reviews: `<!-- midtown: columbus, type: review -->`
- Regular comments: `<!-- midtown: columbus -->` (no type = regular comment, backward compatible)

### Changes needed:

**1. Daemon detection (`src/daemon/helpers.rs`)**
- Update `text_contains_review_signature()` to check for `type: review` in the frontmatter instead of just `<!-- midtown:`
- Keep the `text_has_code_review_header()` and `Reviewed by` checks as fallbacks for backward compatibility with older review comments
- Remove the standalone `text.contains("<!-- midtown:")` check

**2. Agent prompts (`agents/reviewer.md` and/or `agents/common.md`)**
- Update the GitHub comment format for reviews to include `type: review` in the frontmatter
- Regular (non-review) comments keep the existing format unchanged

**3. PR body frontmatter (`agents/coworker.md`)**
- PR bodies use `<!-- midtown: name -->` — these should NOT be detected as reviews (they aren't comments, but verify)

**4. Tests**
- Write failing tests first (per CLAUDE.md)
- Test: comment with `<!-- midtown: columbus -->` (no type) should NOT match as review
- Test: comment with `<!-- midtown: columbus, type: review -->` SHOULD match as review
- Test: comment with `## Code Review by columbus` heading (no frontmatter type) should still match (backward compat)
- Test: comment with both frontmatter type AND heading should match
all_tasks.subject: Fix false positive review detection in text_contains_review_signature

Captured snapshot: snapshot-double-assign-orphan-recovery-20260216-161016.json

Bug: When the daemon restarts and recovers an orphaned task, orphan recovery and task dispatch race within the same tick cycle. Recovery spawns a coworker for the orphaned task, but doesn't mark the task as assigned quickly enough, so dispatch sees it as unassigned and spawns a second coworker for the same task.

Evidence from daemon log (16:04:08-13):
1. 16:04:08 — Orphan recovery detects task !1301, spawns amsterdam (resume=false)
2. 16:04:13 — Task dispatch proposes !1301 for york (already_running=false), spawns york
3. 16:04:13 — WORKTREE COLLISION BLOCKED warning fires, but york is already running

The worktree collision guard prevents the worktree binding but doesn't kill the duplicate session. Both coworkers ran concurrently on the same task — amsterdam opened PR #1150, york discovered it already existed.

Expected: Orphan recovery should mark the task as assigned before task dispatch runs, OR task dispatch should check if recovery already handled the task. The worktree collision guard should also kill the duplicate session if it fires.

Fix approach:
- In the evaluate_tick pipeline, ensure orphan recovery effects are processed (or at least the assignment is recorded) before task dispatch runs
- When WORKTREE COLLISION BLOCKED fires, also emit an Effect to shut down the duplicate coworker

Write a failing test using the captured snapshot, then fix the bug.
all_tasks.subject: Fix race between orphan recovery and task dispatch causing double-assign

2. **headless.rs:HeadlessSession::spawn()**: Change --system-prompt to --append-system-prompt (line ~441).

3. The system prompt content comes from agents::lead_system_prompt() or agents::coworker_system_prompt() depending on the role.

- src/bin/midtown/cli/session.rs:689-783 (build_attach_shell_command, provider_resume_command)
- src/headless.rs:384-500 (HeadlessSession::spawn)

- Verify coworker headless sessions get agents/coworker.md + agents/common.md via --append-system-prompt

## Bug

The daemon's auto-complete logic is too aggressive. It matches tasks to merged PRs based on PR number mentions anywhere in the task description, not just actual task-PR ownership.

Example: A task describing a bug includes context like 'amsterdam opened PR #1150, york discovered it already existed' — the daemon sees PR #1150 is merged and immediately auto-completes the task, even though the task is asking for a FIX to the bug, not tracking that PR.

## Evidence

Tasks !1304, !1305, and !1306 were all auto-completed within ~1 minute of creation because their descriptions mentioned PR #1150 (which was a symptom of the bug they were meant to fix). From the daemon log:

- 16:30:16 — Auto-completing stale task !1304: PR #1150 has been merged
- 16:32:57 — Auto-completing stale task !1305: PR #1150 has been merged

## Expected Behavior

Auto-complete should only trigger when a task's ASSIGNED coworker opened the PR, or when the task is tracked via pr_task_associations. Casual mentions of PR numbers in task descriptions should not trigger auto-completion.

## Key Files

- src/daemon/rules.rs — auto-complete logic (search for auto-complete, stale task, PR merged)
- src/daemon/pr.rs — PR-task association logic

## Fix Approach

Tighten the auto-complete heuristic to only match PRs that are actually associated with the task via pr_task_associations or coworker assignment, not PR numbers found in free-text description fields.
all_tasks.subject: Fix auto-complete heuristic: don't complete tasks based on PR mentions in description

PR #1153 merged without review because:

Timeline:
- 17:01:51: Webhook queued review spawn in 45s
- 17:02:38: Daemon processed pending spawn, but CI still running → no reviewer spawned
- 17:03-17:05: CI went green (all checks passed)
- 17:05:02: Park called in for original task, enabled auto-merge
- 17:06:41: PR merged without review

Root cause: The daemon's review spawn logic runs once (45s after PR opened) and if CI isn't green yet, it doesn't spawn a reviewer. There's no re-evaluation when CI status changes from running → green.

Expected behavior: When CI goes from running → green, the daemon should re-check if the PR needs a reviewer and spawn one if needed.

Investigation needed:
1. Does the webhook handler re-trigger review spawn on CI completion events?
2. Does the polling path detect 'PR ready but no reviewer' condition?
3. Should we queue a retry when the initial spawn attempt fails due to pending CI?

Fix should ensure PRs don't merge without review when auto-merge is enabled.
all_tasks.subject: Fix: Reviewer not spawned when CI passes after initial spawn attempt

Bug: The daemon's reviewer spawn logic is one-shot. If CI isn't green when it checks (45s after PR opens), it never re-evaluates. This allowed a recent PR to merge without review via auto-merge.

Observed behavior:
- PR opens at T+0s
- Daemon queues reviewer spawn for T+45s
- At T+45s, CI still running → no reviewer spawned
- At T+120s, CI goes green
- Daemon never re-checks → PR stays without reviewer
- Author enables auto-merge → immediate merge, no review

Expected behavior: When CI status changes from running → success, daemon should re-evaluate PRs that are ready but have no reviewer assigned.

Fix should address one of:
1. Webhook path: CI completion events trigger review spawn check
2. Polling path: Detect 'PR ready + CI green + no reviewer' and spawn
3. Retry queue: When initial spawn fails due to pending CI, schedule a retry

Note: Do not reference specific PR numbers in the fix - this is a systemic issue.
all_tasks.subject: Daemon review spawn bug: no retry when CI not ready on initial attempt

all_tasks.description:
Bug: The daemon's stale task cleanup in dispatch.rs auto-completes tasks that mention a merged PR anywhere in their subject or description, even when the task is ABOUT that PR (analyzing a bug, investigating an issue) rather than being the work FOR that PR.

Current behavior (dispatch.rs lines 1156-1163 and 1422-1437):
- Calls extract_pr_number() / extract_pr_number_from_task()
- Pattern matches 'PR #NNN' anywhere in subject or description
- If that PR is merged, auto-completes the task
- Causes false positives when tasks reference PRs for context

Recent false positive:
- Task created to fix a bug that occurred during a specific PR
- Task description mentioned the PR number for context
- Daemon auto-completed the task 46 seconds later because that PR was merged
- But the task was about FIXING THE BUG, not about the PR itself

Root cause: Text pattern matching can't distinguish between:
1. 'Task FOR PR #123' (should auto-complete when merged)
2. 'Task ABOUT PR #123' (should NOT auto-complete)

Correct approach:
- Only use the explicit Task.pr field (set via --pr flag or [Midtown !XXX] PR title)
- This field represents 'this task's work is tracked in this PR'
- Pattern matching in subject/description is for grouping sub-tasks, NOT for auto-completion

Fix:
1. Remove extract_pr_number calls from stale task cleanup logic
2. Check task.pr field instead: if task.pr is Some(pr_num) and pr_num is merged, auto-complete
3. Keep extract_pr_number for its other uses (grouping review sub-tasks under same coworker)
all_tasks.subject: Fix stale task cleanup false positives - use explicit pr field, not pattern matching

Several TUI improvements needed:

## 1. Always show channels in the board sidebar (bug fix)
In board.rs, channels only render when they have tasks (lines 46-52, 68-91). The `tasks_by_channel` map is built from the task list, so when there are zero tasks, no channels appear. Fix: always show at least the 'midtown' channel (and any other known channels), even when empty.

## 2. Show same channels as web UI (feature parity)
The web UI fetches channels from a `/channels` API endpoint (fetched in api.js:fetchChannels), which returns all channels including empty ones. The TUI only discovers channels from tasks. The TUI should also fetch the channel list from the daemon (or use the same RPC) so it shows all the same channels the web UI does.

## 3. Clicking a task in the sidebar should attach to that coworker's session
When a task is selected/clicked in the board sidebar, it should attach the user to the coworker session that's working on that task. The task already knows its owner, and `midtown coworker view <name>` or attach functionality exists. Wire up the click/enter action on a task to trigger this.

## 4. Clicking the input box should focus it
Currently clicking on the TUI input area doesn't focus it. Add mouse click handling for the input area to set focus to it.

## 5. Shift+Enter should insert a newline in the TUI input

all_tasks.description:
The embedded PTY in the headed wrapper's RunAgent command doesn't resize when the terminal window is resized.

In src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/headed_wrapper.rs, the RunAgent handler creates a PTY with the initial terminal size (line 700-709):
```rust
let (cols, rows) = crossterm::terminal::size().unwrap_or((120, 40));
let pty_pair = pty_system.openpty(portable_pty::PtySize { rows, cols, ... })
```

But there is no SIGWINCH signal handler to resize the PTY when the terminal window changes size. The `pty_pair.master` has a `resize()` method that needs to be called when the terminal dimensions change.

Fix: Add a signal handler (or crossterm event listener) for terminal resize events in the RunAgent event loop. When a resize is detected, call `pty_pair.master.resize()` with the new dimensions. 

Note: crossterm already provides `Event::Resize(cols, rows)` events which can be used. The master PTY handle will need to be accessible (currently it's partially consumed by `take_writer()` and `try_clone_reader()`, but the master itself should still be available for `resize()`).

Key file: src/bin/midtown/cli/headed_wrapper.rs (RunAgent handler, ~line 686-881)
all_tasks.subject: Fix PTY resize in headed wrapper run-agent

all_tasks.description:
Add a mechanism for coworkers to report their estimated % complete on their current task, and display it in both the TUI and web UI coworker sidebars.

## 1. Progress reporting RPC
Add a way for coworkers to report progress via the midtown CLI, e.g.:
```bash
midtown state progress 25    # 25% complete
midtown state progress 75    # 75% complete
```
Or extend the existing `midtown state` subcommand with a `--progress <0-100>` flag. Store the progress value in the coworker's state in the daemon (alongside phase, task_id, etc.).

## 2. Daemon state + snapshot
Add a `progress: Option<u8>` field (0-100) to the coworker state tracked by the daemon. Include it in WorldSnapshot and the status/kanban RPC responses so the TUI and web UI can read it. Progress should reset to None when a coworker is assigned a new task or goes idle.

## 3. Agent instructions
Update `agents/coworker.md` (or `agents/common.md`) to instruct coworkers to report progress regularly as they work. For example:
- After initial planning/exploration: ~10-20%
- After writing implementation: ~40-60%
- After tests passing: ~70-80%
- After PR opened and CI running: ~90%
- Task complete: 100%

The exact milestones should feel natural, not overly prescriptive.

## 4. TUI display
In src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/ui/board.rs (draw_coworker_status), show progress as a **spinner character + percentage readout** (e.g., `⠋ 45%`) rather than a progress bar — the coworker table is tight on horizontal space. Use braille spinner characters (⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏) that animate on each render tick, paired with the percentage. When no progress is reported, show just the spinner without a percentage.

## 5. Web UI display
Add a progress bar to the coworker status display in the web app sidebar. The web UI has more horizontal space, so a small progress bar or ring is fine here.

Key files:
- src/bin/midtown/cli/state.rs or similar - CLI for reporting progress
- src/daemon/rpc_coworker.rs - RPC handler for progress updates
- src/coworker.rs - coworker state model
- src/daemon/snapshot.rs - WorldSnapshot
- src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/ui/board.rs - TUI coworker sidebar
- src/bin/midtown/cli/chat/app.rs - CoworkerInfo struct
- web-app/src/lib/Sidebar.svelte or similar - web UI sidebar
- agents/coworker.md - agent instructions for reporting progress

Captured snapshot: snapshot-double-assign-open-pr-20260216-231443.json

**Bug**: When a coworker opens a PR and goes idle, the daemon reassigns the task to another coworker, causing duplicate work.

**What happened**:
1. Lexington opened PR #1156 for task !1313, then reported idle
2. reconcile_tasks_in_review() unassigned the task (cleared owner, kept status in_progress)
3. Orphan recovery saw an in_progress task with no active owner and spawned columbus to take over
4. Now two coworkers are working on the same task

**Expected**: Tasks with open PRs should NOT be reassigned. The task is in a valid 'waiting for CI/review' state.

**Fix**: In the orphan recovery logic (dispatch.rs, around the in_progress_tasks_active loop), skip tasks that appear in `snap.tasks_with_open_prs` or `snap.github_open_pr_task_ids`. A task with an open PR doesn't need a new coworker — it's waiting for CI or review.

Key places to check:
- src/daemon/dispatch.rs — orphan recovery logic (look for in_progress_tasks_active)
- src/daemon/snapshot.rs — tasks_with_open_prs, github_open_pr_task_ids
- reconcile_tasks_in_review() already correctly unassigns — the bug is downstream in orphan recovery

Write a failing E2E test using the captured snapshot, then fix the bug.
all_tasks.subject: Fix double-assignment of tasks that already have open PRs

all_tasks.description:
Multiple issues with the lead attach session's environment:

## Problem 1: No --settings-file on attach
The attach path in session.rs:provider_resume_command() (line 791-797) only passes `--continue`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, and `--append-system-prompt`. It does NOT pass `--settings-file`. This means the lead's midtown settings (hooks, env vars, etc.) aren't loaded during interactive attach.

## Problem 2: Lead settings missing enabledPlugins
In settings.rs, `coworker_settings_json()` calls `read_user_plugins()` to include the user's marketplace plugins, but `lead_settings_json()` (line 98-100) does NOT. Even if we fix the settings-file passing, plugins would still be missing for the lead.

## Problem 3: CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID not in attach env
As previously noted, the env var for the shared task list isn't exported in the attach shell command.

## Fix (consolidated approach)
1. In settings.rs: `lead_settings_json()` should also call `read_user_plugins()` and include `enabledPlugins`, same as coworker_settings_json() does.
2. In session.rs: `provider_resume_command()` should write and pass `--settings-file` using `write_lead_settings_file()` (for lead) or `write_coworker_settings_file()` (for coworkers).  
3. Consolidate env var setup: Extract a shared function for env vars (CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID, MIDTOWN_AGENT, etc.) used by both launch.rs and session.rs, so they can't drift.
4. Pass `--setting-sources project,local` for coworker attach sessions (matching the headless config).

Key files:
- src/settings.rs - lead_settings_json() missing enabledPlugins (line 98-100)
- src/bin/midtown/cli/session.rs:762-805 - provider_resume_command() missing --settings-file
- src/bin/midtown/cli/session.rs:689-760 - build_attach_shell_command() missing CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID
- src/launch.rs:332-427 - reference headless env setup for consolidation
- agents/lead-settings.json - lead-specific settings template
- agents/common-settings.json - shared settings template
all_tasks.subject: Set CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID in lead attach session

all_tasks.description:
Nudges (coworker @lead mentions, system messages) are being injected into the lead's PTY while the user is actively typing. The wait_for_nudge_safe() function in headed_wrapper.rs is supposed to prevent this by checking the OutputMirror for the ❯ prompt and active input text, but it's not working.

The mechanism:
- spawn_stdin_relay() tracks keystrokes via update_input_state() 
- wait_for_nudge_safe() checks the OutputMirror (screen output) for the ❯ prompt and input text
- If input is detected, it waits up to COWORKER_INPUT_STABLE_DURATION (20s) for input to settle
- After COWORKER_INPUT_MAX_WAIT (120s), it nudges anyway

Possible causes:
1. The ❯ prompt detection (get_input_text) may not match the current Claude Code TUI prompt format
2. The OutputMirror may not be capturing output correctly in the attach session
3. There's an InputState tracker (stdin side) that could be used instead of/alongside the OutputMirror (stdout side), but wait_for_nudge_safe only checks stdout
4. The timing between output mirror reads and actual screen state could be off

The InputState (stdin-side tracking) knows exactly when the user is typing in real-time. Consider using it as the primary signal instead of parsing terminal output. If input_state.current_input is non-empty and input_state.last_change is recent, the user is typing — don't nudge.

Key file: src/bin/midtown/cli/headed_wrapper.rs
- wait_for_nudge_safe() ~line 478
- update_input_state() ~line 230  
- get_input_text() ~line 417
- RunAgent main loop ~line 786
all_tasks.subject: Fix nudge delivery interrupting user typing in headed wrapper

all_tasks.description:
All reviewer sessions crash immediately after spawn because the daemon's pre-launch hook runs `claude plugin list` which detects the CLAUDECODE env var and fails ('cannot be launched inside another Claude Code session').

**Root cause**: platform_launch.rs runs `claude plugin list/marketplace` commands as a pre-launch hook before each session spawn. The daemon inherits CLAUDECODE from being launched inside Claude Code, causing these subprocess commands to fail. The pre-launch hook logs a warning and continues, but reviewer sessions crash immediately after spawn anyway.

**Fix — move plugin sync to daemon startup**:
1. Move `ensure_claude_plugins_installed()` from the per-spawn pre-launch hook to daemon startup (when `midtown start` / `midtown daemon` runs). At startup time, the environment is clean — no CLAUDECODE is set.
2. Remove the per-spawn pre-launch hook entirely (or make it a no-op that just checks the static flag). Plugin installation only needs to happen once per daemon lifecycle.
3. Also unset CLAUDECODE in the headless session spawn environment (`.env_remove("CLAUDECODE")`) as a safety net — the actual `claude` process shouldn't inherit this from the daemon.

The crash specifically affects reviewers (all of them — lexington, pleasant, broadway, riverside, york, vernon). Dev coworkers get the same warning but survive — investigate why if the startup-time fix doesn't fully resolve it.

Key files:
- src/platform_launch.rs - ensure_claude_plugins_installed() and pre-launch hook
- src/daemon/startup.rs or src/daemon/mod.rs - daemon startup, add plugin sync here  
- src/headless.rs or src/session_manager.rs - headless spawn, unset CLAUDECODE
all_tasks.subject: Fix reviewer sessions crashing due to CLAUDECODE nested session detection
